symptom: An unassigned `CREATE Mod.Region ( Name = 'North' ) COMMIT;` (no `$Var =`) passed `mxcli check --references`, exec reported success, and mxbuild rejected it with CE6005 "The 'Entity' property is required." at the Create object activity (ako/CapTrackV3 FINDINGS §9).
cause: The error names the WRONG property — `Entity` is stored correctly. `mxcli bson dump --compare` of the assigned and unassigned microflows showed one substantive difference in eight: `Action.VariableName` "R" vs "" (the rest were element IDs, flow pointers and StableId). A Mendix Create activity always names its output and Studio Pro supplies the name itself. Fixed by generating one on Studio Pro's New<Entity> convention when the script does not assign, collision-safe against both authored and previously generated names (freshCreateVariable/variableNameTaken, with a generatedVars set on flowBuilder).
insight: Do not trust which property a Mendix CE names. CE6005 said Entity was missing while Entity was present and VariableName was empty; chasing the named property would have found nothing wrong. `bson dump --compare` between a working and a failing document settles it in one step and is the right first move for any 'mxbuild rejects what we wrote' report — it reduced this to one field out of eight diffs. Supplying the value rather than refusing is right here precisely because nothing is guessed: the author asked to create an object and not for a handle, which is what an auto-named output is. The generated name is deliberately NOT registered in varTypes, so it stays unreferenceable and `change $NewRegion` remains the error it is.
